title: Quant Overledger: Whitepaper v0.1
lede: The original gateway-OS argument: applications should not be trapped on a single ledger. Historical document, not a product spec.

title: Blockchain a business solution in the Bitcoin Era
lede: Master’s thesis in Computer Engineering (rel. Elio Piccolo), placed at UCL’s Centre for Blockchain Technologies — the same centre Tasca directed. Full text is secretated on PoliTo WebThesis; bibliographic record only.

title: Overledger Network Treasury
lede: Treasury and network-design note from the whitepaper era. Not evidence of a live token economy.

title: Do You Need a Distributed Ledger Technology Interoperability Solution?
lede: The academic paper behind Overledger’s taxonomy. Modes (data transfer, asset transfer, asset exchange) × infrastructure (nodes, proxies, gateways). Quant’s product claim sits in the gateway cell.

title: A Survey on Blockchain Interoperability: Past, Present, and Future Trends
lede: The canonical literature review (284 papers + grey literature). Public connectors, blockchain engines, hybrid connectors. Context for SATP and Cacti, not a Quant SKU.

title: SoK: Security and Privacy of Blockchain Interoperability
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
lede: Systematisation of knowledge on what actually breaks when two ledgers talk. The security case for a standard gateway protocol rather than a zoo of bridges.

title: A Brief History of Blockchain Interoperability
lede: Why interoperability is needed and what a decade of attempts actually produced. Academic corridor (Lisbon–Boston), not a product brochure.

title: DLT interoperability: what are the options?
lede: WEF-shaped categories compared on resilience, decentralisation and UX. Riley’s conclusion: API gateway, and Overledger as the instance Quant ships.

title: Enabling the Internet of Value
lede: How blockchain connects global businesses. The philosophical library behind ‘network of networks’.

title: Banking Beyond Banks and Money
lede: What happens when money leaves the branch. Pre-Overledger academic context.

title: Internet of Value: A Risky Necessity
lede: Opinion essay: a value layer on the internet is coming; governance risk is the price of admission.

title: Flow Applications: build once, deploy everywhere
lede: Overledger workflows that the same human UI, HTTP client or MCP-compatible agent can call.

title: The three-layer digital money architecture
lede: Wholesale CBDC, tokenised deposits, public-chain stablecoins — plus a horizontal interoperability layer. Quant’s published map of the future of money, not a central-bank paper.

title: Secure Asset Transfer Protocol (SATP) Core
lede: Standards-track draft. Gateway-to-gateway asset transfer. Not a Quant SKU.

title: Secure Asset Transfer architecture
lede: Architecture companion to SATP core.

title: Open Digital Asset Protocol (ODAP)
lede: The 2020 precursor that became SATP. Same gateway-to-gateway shape; different name.

title: Adapting SATP for Secure Cross-Network Asset Exchange
lede: UCL master’s work supervised by Riley: how SATP’s transfer machine can be adapted for exchange, not only transfer. Academic adjacency, not a product spec.

title: ISO/TS 23516:2026 — DLT interoperability framework
lede: Framework for interoperability between DLT systems and entities outside them. Verdian convened WG7; the standard is ISO’s, not a product.

title: ISO/TC 307 — Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies
lede: The committee Verdian proposed in 2015. Landscape for every interoperability conversation on this map.

title: Blockchain communications and ordering (US11842335B2)
lede: Granted method for chronologically ordering transactions from different blockchains. Assigned to Quant Network Ltd.

title: US20200311718A1 — application publication
lede: Application that became US11842335B2. Useful for the claim set as originally published.

title: Japanese patent — multi-DLT token / Fusion rollup
lede: Quant’s note on Japanese acceptance covering updates across two or more ledgers — the Fusion rollup claim.

title: Vocalink / Mastercard payment patents (Hargreaves)
lede: Two Vocalink-era filings Quant’s people page cites: data-processing / merchant-mandate review, and international ACH with addressing. Payments rails before DLT.

title: Quant selected for UK tokenised sterling deposits
lede: 26 September 2025. UK Finance and six banks select Quant to provide GBTD infrastructure. Overledger + PayScript. Not a CBDC.

title: UK Finance live GBTD pilot announcement
lede: Primary official-sector announcement. Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, NatWest, Nationwide, Santander; Quant, EY, Linklaters supporting.

title: Quant on Project Rosalind (BIS × Bank of England)
lede: Concluded experiment. Quant says it was on the vendor team with UST. BIS is explicit: not BoE policy, not a launch.

title: Project Rosalind — CBDC API prototypes
lede: Primary official-sector page. Retail-CBDC API experiment run with the Bank of England. Treat as concluded lab work.

title: Oracle Blockchain Platform Digital Assets Edition
lede: Oracle names Quant Overledger as the orchestration layer for cross-ledger unified-ledger workflows. Hyperledger Fabric underneath.

title: Connecting agentic AI payments to the banking system
lede: Quant joins the Linux Foundation x402 Foundation. Fusion Layer 2.5 claimed x402-ready. Agents settling in tokenised bank money is the thesis, not a live CBDC.

title: Quant in the Bank of England Synchronisation Lab
lede: Industry experimentation in a simulated RT2 environment. Quant’s own note says this is not BoE endorsement, policy or a live deployment.

title: Murex × Quant — tokenised deposits in MX.3
lede: 25 March 2026. Overledger lets MX.3 talk to multiple ledgers for tokenised deposits and digital bonds.

title: Bank tokenization and global payments
lede: Landscape survey on tokenised deposits and wholesale payments.

title: RTGS synchronisation — desk research note
venue: Desk file · BoE language, not a Quant SKU
lede: Desk research on Bank of England RTGS synchronisation language. Distinct from Quant’s February 2026 Synchronisation Lab participation (simulated RT2). This file is not a Bank of England publication naming Quant as operator of Synthorus.

title: Gilbert Verdian — public biography pack
lede: Public-source pack used to keep the People chapter honest.

title: Hyperledger In-depth: categorisation of DLT interoperability
lede: Riley’s 2021 public walkthrough of the same taxonomy as the Quant research note, hosted by Hyperledger.

title: Voting over a Distributed Ledger: An interdisciplinary perspective
lede: Riley’s King’s College years: what a ledger can and cannot do for elections. Pre-Quant academic work, not an Overledger feature.

title: Using distributed ledger technology for shareholder rights management
lede: AAMAS paper from the KCL voting-and-governance lab. How a permissioned ledger can record shareholder rights — adjacency to programmable assets, not a Quant product.

title: Towards a Design Philosophy for Interoperable Blockchain Systems
lede: MIT Connection Science: interoperability as a design philosophy, not a bridge. Same year as the Overledger whitepaper; same problem, different room.

title: Toward an Interoperability Architecture for Blockchain Autonomous Systems
lede: IEEE TEMS special issue. The architecture paper SATP’s gateway model sits next to. MIT, not Quant.

title: Blockchain Gateways, Bridges and Delegated Hash-Locks
lede: Why a gateway is not a bridge. The vocabulary SATP later standardises.

title: Hermes: Fault-tolerant middleware for blockchain interoperability
lede: Academic middleware paper. Cousin to Cacti and SATP, not a Quant SKU.

title: SATP gateway recovery
lede: How a SATP gateway resumes a transfer after a crash. Individual draft, not a Quant product.

title: Protocol for requesting and sharing views across networks
lede: IBM Research SATP adjacency: how two networks share a view of state. Complements core transfer.

title: Secure Asset Transfer use cases
lede: Why anyone would run SATP: the use-case draft from IBM Research.

title: Hyperledger Cacti whitepaper
lede: LF Decentralized Trust’s enterprise interoperability project. Belchior maintains it. Open-source neighbour of Overledger, not a Quant SKU.

title: SATP Implementation Guide
lede: How a SATP gateway actually locks, burns, mints and commits on the networks it represents. Methodology for implementers, not a Quant SKU.

title: Secure Asset Exchange Protocol
lede: Lock-and-assign instead of burn-and-mint: SATP’s cousin for exchange rather than transfer.

title: Authenticated Delegation and Authorized AI Agents
lede: Extends OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect with agent-specific credentials. The ethics constraint next to Flow/MCP and x402. MIT, not a Quant product.
